description:
Single 3D points and directions are passed around as float[3] / double[3] (packed xyz, read as p[0], p[1], p[2]) in about 60 places where a JOML Vector3f (or Vector3d) belongs. Replace them, and settle how Vector3f arithmetic is written across Ixdar.

Starting point: the user began this conversion by hand inside the CRAW-112 worktree (the ray-cast chain): Camera3D view rays, TriangleBvh ray queries, TriangleGeometry axis-ray crossings, SurfacePicker (a Vector3f `point` instead of pointX/Y/Z), SurfaceWaypoints.format(List<Vector3f>), RingDslWriter (List<Vector3f> splines, Vector3f base normal), RingScene cursorPoint / cursorRayOrigin / cursorRayDirection / anchorPixel, RingRegionTool.pickedPoints, RingRegions.nearestActiveFace(Vector3f), SelectCommand, LabelCommand, Pick, Project, SculptSync, HalfEdgeMeshRuntime, MeshLabels and BisectorTest. That work is unfinished and does not compile (e.g. `Vector3f direction = new float[...]`, `camera.worldPerPixel(cursorPoint.x)`, `nearestActiveFace(point.x,point.y,point.z)`); it was moved into this ticket's worktree to be finished here.

Remaining sites (from a grep of float[]/double[] used as single points or directions):
- Coons handle maps: CoonsExtrudeMeshNode, CoonsInsetFacesNode, CoonsLoopCutNode (maps of float[3] handles, often copied out of a Vector3f).
- Sculpt and rays: StrokeSketch (center, origin/direction), KeyCandidates, ReferenceStrokes, SilhouetteStroke, StrokeElementGrid, DisplacementSum.seedDragXyz, RayBatch.origin/direction, NearestVertex.origin.
- Curvature: ImplicitFit (double[3] normals and steps), PrincipalDirectionField, CrestLineDetector, SaddlePointDetector, SurfaceRidges.seconds.
- Segmentation: SemanticPatchDecomposer, PatchBoundaryWalker, MscCellAssembly.
- Skeleton: MeshSkeletonComparator, MeshSkeletonExtractor.
- Mesh repair and analysis: MeshRepair, MeshDistance.
- Rings: RegionExplosion, Pick, SurfaceWaypoints.
- Other: ReferenceOutlines (extents, point), ShadingEdges, FitReferencesNode, TradeRouteTool.

Not in scope (3-tuples that are not points): barycentric weights (ChartBarycentric), uv/angle frames (ChartAtlas, FaceSegmentIndex, PatchBoundaryBuilder, SeamlessDofSystem), priority-queue entries (FlipGeodesics), hex q/r/s (PointND), scalar triples (DiscreteGradient), TradeScene loop. Packed n-point arrays (new float[XYZ * n], per-face centroid tables, GPU buffers) stay packed.

Out-parameters: the user does not allow `Vector3f out` / `dest` parameters (e.g. MeshTopology.faceCentroid(int, Vector3f out)). Methods converted here return a new vector instead of filling an argument. MeshTopology.vertexPosition(int, Vector3f dest) has ~367 callers; report on it rather than converting it here unless it falls out naturally.

Analysis part: survey the Vector3f/Vector3d code that does arithmetic element by element today (`a.x - b.x`, `a.y - b.y`, `a.z - b.z`; dot and cross products spelled out; lerps, centroids, distance-squared written by hand) and say which could be one JOML call or one shared helper. Then answer whether Ixdar should wrap Vector3f in its own IxVector class to add common operations (and to get immutable/value semantics instead of JOML's mutate-in-place style that drives out-parameters), with the trade-offs: allocation and GC cost in hot loops, JOML interop with the renderer and math code, how many call sites would change, and what a wrapper's API would be. Write the findings on the ticket; do not build IxVector in this ticket, propose it as a follow-up if recommended.

Widened after review (no follow-up tickets): also (a) keep SurfacePicker's ray parameter in double so the hit point rounds once, as before; (b) convert the rest of the spline writer family (RingDslWriter.appendSpline, splineStatement, ConfirmedRing.baseNormal) to Vector3f; (c) add a returning MeshTopology.vertexPosition(int) and move the callers outside hot loops onto it; (d) add a static Vectors helper for reading and writing one point of a packed float[] and migrate the hand-written p[i*3], p[i*3+1], p[i*3+2] triples to it; (e) replace the hand-written sub/dot/cross/lengthSquared on Vector3f with JOML calls, accepting last-ulp differences from Math.fma, with tests tolerant of that.
definition-of-done:
1. The user's partial ray-chain conversion moved from CRAW-112 is finished and compiles.
2. Every listed point/direction site uses Vector3f or Vector3d instead of float[3]/double[3]; any site deliberately left is listed on the ticket with the reason.
3. No new out-parameters: converted methods return their vector.
4. The elementwise-arithmetic survey and the IxVector recommendation (yes/no, API sketch, cost) are written on the ticket.
5. The full build (checkstyle included) and the unit tests pass; behaviour is unchanged (ring picking, BVH ray queries, Coons handles, sculpt rays).
6. A launch entry and screenshot show the ring scene picking and drawing a ring as before.

7. Items (a) to (e) of the widened description are done; any site left is listed on the ticket with its reason.

What to do with MeshTopology.vertexPosition(int, Vector3f dest), the out-parameter with ~367 callers
changes-made: Finished the user's ray-chain conversion (Camera3D, TriangleBvh, TriangleGeometry, SurfacePicker, SurfaceWaypoints, RingDslWriter callers, RingScene, RingRegionTool, RingRegions, SelectCommand, LabelCommand, Pick, Project, SculptSync, HalfEdgeMeshRuntime, MeshLabels, BisectorTest): it compiles and every test passes. Fixes inside it: TriangleBvh's `normal.component,(...)` became setComponent; RingRegionTool's reselect wrote only the first picked point (single-term format(pickedPoints, 1)) and now writes one point term per picked point, as before; RingScene.cursorPoint/cursorRayDirection are initialised so they are never null. Added: MeshTopology.faceCentroid(int) returning a new Vector3f (summing corner/count in the old RingRegionTool order, so values are bit-identical); HalfEdgeMeshRuntime.projectToPixels(Camera3D, Vector3f) returning the pixel or null; RingTool.positionOf(int); MeshLabels.add(String, Vector3f); SurfaceWaypoints.points(float[]) and format(float[], int) for packed n-point arrays.

Converted beyond the user's chain: StrokeSketch.center and its rays (and StrokeKeyRoute, MultiviewScreenshot, OutlineCompare, SilhouetteHullNode, FitReferencesNode, PlaceInCellNode, RegionLayer, StrokeLift); RayBatch.origin/direction (MeshProjection, MeshSmoothing); DisplacementSum.visibility; KeyCandidates; ReferenceStrokes; SilhouetteStroke drag; VoxelGrid.longestRunMiddle/nearest; MeshRepair (containment-ray origin as Vector3d, castBackRays, meetsAxisLine, sealedIn); Patch.centroid (record field now Vector3f; MscCellAssembly, SemanticPatchDecomposer, PatchDecomposerCLI); PatchBoundaryWalker.unitDir; the Coons directed-handle maps (CoonsHandleBuilder.flushDirectedHandles now takes Map<Long, Vector3f>; CoonsExtrudeMeshNode, CoonsInsetFacesNode, CoonsLoopCutNode). double[] points became Vector3d (MeshRepair ray origin, TriangleBvh faceRange centre/normal) to keep their precision. Behaviour kept exact: JOML div(float) multiplies by the reciprocal, so averages are written x/n per component; JOML dot/distance/fma use Math.fma, so hand-written dot products stayed hand-written where the old code was not fused.

Reused scratch vectors kept (no new per-iteration allocation): RayBatch.Rays per-worker origin/direction (one per worker, refilled per ray); TriangleBvh.hemisphereEscapes ray direction (refilled per hemisphere ray); TriangleBvh.faceRange centre/normal and lineThrough(int, Vector3d, Vector3d) (per triangle in the BVH build; lineThrough keeps the user's fill-the-argument shape there, the only out-parameter left, because a returned vector would allocate twice per triangle); MeshRepair.castBackRays centroid/back; StrokeLift liftedPoint; SilhouetteStroke best; MeshLabels.resolve/unlabel position; MeshSmoothing/MeshProjection rays. Camera3D.rayThroughPixel(..., Vector3f origin, Vector3f direction) is the user's own two-result fill and was left as written.

Sites deliberately left on float[]/double[], with reasons: (1) GirdlingPlane / PlaneSurfaceLoop point and viewDirection, Preview.hitPoint/previewHitPoint: deep cascade through the closed-ring girdle search; ClosedRingTool wraps at the boundary. (2) NearestVertex.origin, VoxelGrid.origin, MeshDistance and MeshSkeletonComparator bounding boxes, MeshSkeletonExtractor.toWorld: read and written by axis index in per-axis loops; Vector3f.get(int)/setComponent are switches, and JOML min/max use Math.min/max whose NaN and -0 handling differs from the `<` comparisons. (3) PrincipalDirectionField.dirMax/dirMin(v, float[] out), CrestLineDetector, SaddlePointDetector, buildTangentBasis, ImplicitFit normal/step/shape, SurfaceRidges.seconds: per-vertex hot paths over packed fields; converting forces either an out-parameter (banned) or an allocation per step. (4) DisplacementSum.seedDragXyz (packed n), eyeForward (6-tuple), ReferenceOutlines.extents/forward (feeds packed view-axis tables), RegionExplosion weighted sums (packed per region), StrokeElementGrid.key, TradeRouteTool points (2D op payload): packed or not single points. (5) ShadingEdges normal is a 3x3 system, out of scope. (6) Spline writers are half-converted: the user made RingDslWriter.replaceSpline/appendBisector take List<Vector3f> (callers wrap packed arrays with SurfaceWaypoints.points); appendSpline, splineStatement and ConfirmedRing.baseNormal (58 uses) are still float[]. User to decide whether to convert the whole spline family. (7) SurfacePicker: the user changed the hit `parameter` from double to float, which can round differently; left as written, flagged for review.

MeshTopology.vertexPosition(int, Vector3f dest): 368 call sites, not converted. Almost all are inside per-vertex or per-face loops that reuse one scratch Vector3f; a returning version would allocate per call there (escape analysis removes some but not across the interface call). Recommendation: keep it as the one sanctioned out-parameter, and add a returning `Vector3f vertexPosition(int)` default only for the cold callers (UI, picking, one-shot queries) in a follow-up, migrating those by hand.

Elementwise survey (ixdar-app main): spelled-out a.x-b.x/a.y-b.y subtraction on Vector3f in 11 lines and hand dot products on Vector3f in 7, together in 11 files (most in RouteNetwork, Camera3D, SDFLine, PatchBoundaryWalker; also MeshNodeViewerScene, SDFBezier, StrokeSketch, MidpointSplit, MeshSkeletonExtractor, IrregularQuadLayoutGenerator, Bridge); hand dot products on float[] indices 15; hand cross products 4; hand length-squared x*x+y*y+z*z about 120, nearly all on scalars pulled out of packed arrays. The Vector3f ones map to sub/dot/cross/lengthSquared, but JOML's dot, distance, length and fma use Math.fma, so each swap changes results in the last ulp; do it as its own ticket with tests that tolerate that. The bigger pattern is packed-array access (p[i*3], p[i*3+1], p[i*3+2]) around single points: a shared static helper (read a Vector3f at index i from a packed float[], write one back, per-axis bounds) would remove most of the hand-written triples without changing arithmetic.

IxVector recommendation: no wrapper class. Costs: Vector3f appears 1479 times in 202 main files and the renderer, Camera3D, Matrix4f.transformPosition and MeshTopology all speak JOML, so a wrapper means conversions at every boundary or a rewrite of all of them; an immutable value wrapper allocates per operation in hot loops (BVH build, smoothing, sculpt deposit) where JOML's mutate-in-place reuses scratch, and Java has no value types yet to make that free; a mutable wrapper adds nothing JOML lacks. JOML already has sub, add, fma, lerp, dot, cross, distance, normalize, min/max, setComponent/get(int) and Vector3d. What is missing is small and static: a `Vectors` helper with `Vector3f at(float[] packed, int i)`, `void store(Vector3f v, float[] packed, int i)` and per-axis bounds, plus the returning vertexPosition(int) above. Proposed follow-ups: (a) the Vectors helper and migrating packed-triple sites; (b) the ulp-tolerant swap of hand dot/cross/sub to JOML calls; (c) converting the rest of the spline writer family. If Java value classes (Valhalla) land, revisit an immutable IxVector then.

Widened scope, done in this ticket: (a) SurfacePicker keeps the ray parameter in double and rounds the hit point once, as before the conversion. (b) The spline writer family is Vector3f end to end: RingDslWriter.append/appendSpline/splineStatement/statement take List<Vector3f> anchors and a Vector3f base normal; ConfirmedRing.baseNormal, RingTool.draftBaseNormal and savedNormalByStatement, RingToolState.draftBaseNormal, ClosedRingTool.previewPlaneNormal, AuthoredSplineRing.trace/insert/refitGeodesic/fitPlane and SplineRingNode take Vector3f; SurfaceWaypoints.point(String) reads one point or null; RingTool.written(float[]) returns Vector3f. AuthoredSplineRing.planeNormal stays float[] because it feeds PlaneSurfaceLoop, the girdle family left on the ticket. (c) MeshTopology.vertexPosition(int) returns a new vector (default method); 24 one-shot callers moved to it (Pick, SliverCollapse, CoonsHandleBuilder, NearestVertex, DisplacementSum, SpherizeMeshNode, PlayerSpawner, CoonsExtrudeMeshNode, CoonsLoopCutNode, RingTool, AssignBezierHandlesNode and 11 test sites); per-vertex loops keep vertexPosition(int, Vector3f). (d) PackedPoints (geometry.mesh.data.representation) with at(float[], offset) and store(float[]/double[], offset, Vector3f): 110 hand-written triples across 64 files moved to it. The ~45 v.set(a[i], a[i+1], a[i+2]) refills of scratch vectors stay: JOML has no offset setter, and a helper would be either an out-parameter or an allocation per step. AlignRotationToVectorNode writes quaternions and stays. (e) Hand-written vector math swapped for JOML: Camera3D basis (normalize/cross), PatchBoundaryWalker dots, NDirectionField and CurvatureConstraints edge vectors, dihedral cross and distances, MeshNodeViewerScene occluder test, MeshTopology diagonal comparison, Color.distanceTo, QuadLayoutOverlay edge length. Scalar-heavy blocks that build cross products from packed scalars (QuadLayoutOverlay face frame, SDFLine 2D) stay. The user accepted last-ulp differences; the existing suite is the check.

Second sweep: single 3-vectors moved from float[3] to Vector3f across curvature (PrincipalDirectionField, CrestLineDetector, SaddlePointDetector, LimbAxis), path queries (PlaneSurfaceLoop, GirdlingPlane, SurfaceConnection, SurfacePathCrossings, NearestVertex), SurfaceGeodesics/SurfaceSplineTracer, AuthoredSplineRing, ring tools and Item/Preview, Camera3D/PointVisibility projection (returns Vector3f pixel+depth or null), skeleton extractor/comparator records, ReferenceOutlines, MeshDistance, SculptStroke, MeshSegmenter, VoxelGrid origin, OutlineCompare centreShift. Packed n-point buffers, per-vertex scalars, Jacobians and 2D pixel arrays stay float[].

Wider survey (supersedes the narrower elementwise survey above as the ticket's survey item). Representations: Ixdar needs no vector type of its own; JOML covers single values (Vector3f, Vector3d where precision matters, Vector2f/2d for uv). Two gaps are types, not vectors: many points travel as bare float[] or ArrayList<Float> (fixed by ENG-44's PackedPoints object), and frames travel as float[9] (TriangleBvh.hemisphereBasis), out-parameters (CrossField) or loose t1/t2 pairs where Matrix3f belongs (used in 1 file today). 2D still mixes Vector2f (45 files), new float[2] (18 files) and scalar ax/ay pairs. Repeated operations: angle by acos(dot) in about 12 places, half without clamping to [-1, 1] (SemanticPatchDecomposer x3, PatchBoundaryWalker, PatchDecomposerCLI, HalfEdgeMesh:1440), which gives NaN when rounding pushes the dot past 1, where JOML Vector3f.angle clamps; corner angle on a packed buffer three times (PatchDecomposerCLI.triAngle, SemanticPatchDecomposer.triangleAngle, HalfEdgeMesh); triangle normal in HalfEdgeMesh/ArrayMesh.faceNormal, QuadLayoutOverlay.faceNormal (out-parameter), AttachToSurfaceNode.faceNormal and MeshRepair.unitNormal; triangle area in TriangleGeometry.area, MeshHoleFiller.triangleArea and PatchRectangleMap, beside the existing MeshTopology.faceArea; tangent frame from a normal in about 14 files, each choosing its own helper axis; removing the normal component (v - n dot(n, v)) 15 lines in 7 files; sqrt(x*x+y*y+z*z) 50 lines in 28 files, mostly on values pulled out of packed arrays; centroid and lerp loops (51 and 13 files) mostly one-offs. No new helper classes: the triangle and frame operations go on PackedPoints and MeshTopology in ENG-44, the angle and normal-removal sites become JOML calls (angle, fma). Barycentric weights stay double[]: three scalars, not a point.

Timing against master (0b8b45f5, both trees alternated on one machine): ring-tool hover frame, ring-region update and extraction unchanged, with identical hover fingerprints and mesh-repair report. Mesh repair had run about 15% slower; JFR put it in MeshRepair.castBackRays and TriangleBvh.lineThrough, where per-component Vector3f.setComponent loops had replaced plain array writes. Both now set the three components directly (same float arithmetic), and nearestHitAvoiding reads the ray origin into float locals before traversal. After: repair median 1.80 s against master's 1.79 s over five alternating runs. The SculptSync, PixelPickProject and Bisector unit-test gaps in the full suite were test-order noise: run alone they overlap master.
review-summary: Single points and directions now travel as JOML Vector3f or Vector3d instead of packed float[3] arrays, finishing the user's ray-picking conversion and extending it to sculpt rays, mesh repair, segmentation and Coons handles. Named vectors read and compose with JOML instead of index juggling.
